content:
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. In my current work as a QA Automation Engineer at Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines and automate Kubernetes-based test environments used by three teams. I’m looking to build further on this infrastructure experience, and the opportunity to help shape the platform connecting a new train fleet with cloud services is particularly compelling.

At Odrava, I built merge-request environments with an application, PostgreSQL, and seeded data, deployed through Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster. I automated their cleanup and enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against the environments. I also profiled CI pipelines across three teams, reducing average run time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly runner costs by about 30%. To make test quality more visible, I built a Python and PostgreSQL process and Grafana dashboards that helped teams reduce the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.

My infrastructure experience includes namespace-level work on a Kubernetes cluster operated by a platform team, TLS certificate management with cert-manager in a personal k3s and GitOps project, and provisioning a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform. I have also built familiarity with AWS EC2 and S3 fundamentals through learning. I document technical processes for others—in my current role, I wrote the CI guide used for onboarding—and have mentored two QA interns. These experiences have strengthened my ability to make infrastructure easier to use, review and operate collaboratively.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in CI/CD, Kubernetes test infrastructure, automation and observability could contribute to Corvale’s fleet connectivity work. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, concise, and well structured. It uses strong quantified evidence: pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, CI runner costs reduced by about 30%, and flaky-test rate reduced from 7% to below 1%. It also accurately distinguishes workplace Kubernetes responsibilities from personal infrastructure work, avoiding overclaiming cluster ownership or production AWS experience. The main content limitation is that the final letter remains somewhat general about systems design, technical leadership, and security, although the candidate's documented experience does not fully establish all of those requirements.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-readable: it uses standard paragraphs, a conventional greeting and closing, and relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, PostgreSQL, Python, Grafana, Terraform, TLS, cert-manager, and AWS EC2/S3. AI screening probability is moderate to good for the infrastructure-adjacent aspects of the role, especially Kubernetes, CI/CD, automation, observability, and measurable improvement. Screening will be limited for the employer's central terms—Terragrunt, mTLS, systems architecture, production cloud operations, and fleet or remote-device connectivity—because the candidate's original information does not support most of them. The Terraform and AWS claims are appropriately qualified, which improves credibility.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with Corvale's engineering-led and collaborative culture through evidence of ownership, cross-team enablement, documentation, onboarding support, and mentoring. It presents a credible transition from QA automation into infrastructure and DevOps work. The strongest role alignment is hands-on Kubernetes test infrastructure, CI/CD optimization, observability, TLS certificate management, and Terraform-based personal infrastructure. The candidate has material gaps against strong Terraform and Terragrunt, mTLS, formal systems architecture, IoT or remote-device integration, backend/full-stack development, and Linux/virtual-machine experience. AWS is present only at learning/fundamentals level rather than professional production level. These are candidate-experience gaps, not defects that can be fixed through wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the third paragraph, make the personal-project infrastructure evidence more concrete by changing the sentence beginning "My infrastructure experience includes" to: "My infrastructure experience includes namespace-level work on a Kubernetes cluster operated by a platform team, and a personal three-node k3s GitOps project where I provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and configured Argo CD, Traefik ingress, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, and cert-manager for TLS certificate management." This uses supported experience and better surfaces GitOps, infrastructure provisioning, and observability keywords.
2. In the third paragraph, replace "I have also built familiarity with AWS EC2 and S3 fundamentals through learning" with "I have developed AWS EC2 and S3 fundamentals through self-directed learning, without professional AWS production experience." This is more precise and prevents the statement from being interpreted as production cloud experience.
3. In the final paragraph, make the analytical and collaborative value proposition more specific by changing the sentence beginning "I would welcome" to: "I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience optimizing CI/CD, building Kubernetes test infrastructure, improving observability, and documenting operating practices could contribute to Corvale's fleet connectivity work." This ties the closing more directly to evidence already presented without claiming fleet or production-platform experience.
